thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: autoscaler ceiling reached for gpu-pool-west (max nodes hit) - queue growth detected · severity: high

oncall-tess: acked. Seeing a spike in generation queue for the west cluster, requests getting 429 / throttled.
sre-jack: i'm on it. can someone paste current queue/backlog metrics?
eng-ml-kate: from dashboards: request queue length ~ 48, enqueue rate 12 req/s, avg wait 18s, 429s increasing. Model-serving pods staying saturated; node count at configured max 120.
support-ali: we already got two customer escalations in EU-west and US-west. they're seeing timeouts and failed chat completions.
infra-lee: confirmed node group 'gpu-pool-west' at max size 120, autoscaler can't add more due to maxNodes setting. Policy says safety cap 120 for cost reasons.
oncall-tess: quick triage: impact is user-facing for hosted API (generation/chat) in west. Can we temporarily raise the max while we stabilize? Need decision and owner.
sre-jack: propose manual cap bump to 170 (temporary). infra-lee do you have clearance to perform?
infra-lee: I have permission for emergency bump, but need oncall approval from product or SRE lead. cto-maya, can you sign off?
cto-maya: sign-off for emergency bump to 170 for the next 2 hours. prioritize customer availability.
sre-jack: ok infra-lee, please run the scale. call out exact steps so we have an audit trail.
infra-lee: plan: 1) update autoscaler maxNodes for nodepool gpu-pool-west from 120 -> 170 via cloud console/CLI; 2) monitor pod scheduling and queue drain; 3) if any pods fail to start, rollback to 120 and open a followup. executing now.
infra-lee: running: `gcloud container node-pools update gpu-pool-west --cluster=redwood-west --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=10 --max-nodes=170`  (running in project: redwood-prod)
incident-bot: DEPLOYMENT CHECK: new autoscaler config submitted by infra-lee · status: in-progress
sre-jack: watching cluster events: `kubectl get nodes -w`
eng-ml-kate: model-serving pods pending -> most resolving as new nodes come up. latency metrics starting to drop slightly.
support-ali: customers on the thread confirm reduced errors for one of the escalations (thanks). still seeing a couple of 504s.
infra-lee: cloud console shows node pool scaling up +40 nodes already, target reaching ~160.
oncall-tess: keep an eye on quota limits (vCPUs, GPUs). if we hit cloud account quota we may need a different plan.
infra-lee: checking quotas: GPU quota available is enough for +60 nodes for west (we're ok).
sre-jack: logs show kube-scheduler events for preemption? Not preempting, just backlog of pods scheduling until nodes finish joining.
eng-ml-kate: temporarily enable soft-fallback policy: route low-priority requests to smaller model-quantized endpoints to reduce pressure. I can flip routing flag if we need.
oncall-tess: do it. eng-ml-kate, please announce when toggled.
eng-ml-kate: flipped `route: low-priority -> model-small-quant` in feature flags. Should reduce token throughput ~30% for batch jobs.
support-ali: customers reporting improvement, still monitoring.
incident-bot: QUEUE METRICS: queue length trending down: 48 -> 15 in last 8 minutes. throttle rate 429% -> 6% (approx).
sre-jack: nice. continue to monitor for stabilization period (30m). we should document exact change for postmortem: who approved, commands, timestamps.
infra-lee: update: autoscaler maxNodes now set to 170; current node count 162; no quota alerts. saving CLI output for audit: `Operation XXXXXX`
oncall-tess: start a followup ticket in incidents-triage with priority P1 -> include affected customers, duration, the emergency cap bump, and rollback plan?
sre-jack: created ticket: INC-1732110001 (emergency gpu-pool-west cap bump). linking logs and deploy CLI output.
cto-maya: two asks: 1) set a rollback criterion: if error rate spikes or cost exceed threshold, revert to 120; 2) post-incident runbook to review why autoscaler couldn't handle the surge.
oncall-tess: noted. rollback criterion: if request latency > 2x baseline or error rate > 5% sustained for 10m.
eng-ml-kate: scheduling a quick eval on model-serving behavior under higher node counts (why didn't autoscaler respond earlier?).
sre-jack: suspicion: pod eviction/taint interplay + burst of small jobs causing slow scale decisions. we need to capture pod events and CA logs.
support-ali: customers asked for ETA on permanent fix. recommended response: "we performed an emergency capacity increase to restore service; engineering is investigating root cause and will follow up within 48 hours".
infra-lee: cleanup plan: reduce maxNodes back to 120 in 2 hours if metrics stable for 30m. will not forcibly drain nodes; will let autoscaler reduce naturally.
sre-jack: monitoring window: 30m stable, then schedule controlled rollback. assign oncall for rollback: oncall-tess.
oncall-tess: ack. I'll coordinate when it's safe.
incident-bot: NOTE: audit log entry created: user=infra-lee action=update-autoscaler target=gpu-pool-west from=120 to=170 op=Operation-XXXXXX ts=1732110205
frac: (bot-like message) reminder: create postmortem and link to INC-1732110001.
sre-jack: short-term postmortem outline in ticket: root-cause hypothesis, timeline, mitigation steps, followups (scale policy change, better early-warning marginal slope alerts, quota pre-warm), owners assigned.
eng-ml-kate: will run targeted load test against autoscaler behavior in staging to reproduce.
cto-maya: please include cost impact estimate in the followup brief. executive team flagged for transparency.
support-ali: sending customer update now.
infra-lee: 2hr timer started for temporary cap. will post final status on rollback or extension.
oncall-tess: thanks everyone. tagging for handoff: oncall-tess remains owner until rollback complete, sre-jack for monitoring, infra-lee for infra ops, eng-ml-kate for model routing changes, support-ali for customer comms.
incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED: autoscaler ceiling mitigated; manual cap bump applied. followup ticket INC-1732110001 created.
noncall-tess: final note: will capture this thread and paste into postmortem doc. if anything regresses ping me directly. :thumbsup:
cto-maya: thanks team. good quick coordination.
